## Pillar 3 — Generate *(the heart of the exercise)*
- **Must:** from chat, user has the brain **generate a document** grounded in the KB. Pick one use case: **candidate profile** / **comparison of candidates in a search** / **exec or portco brief**. One is enough.
- **Must:** the generated document is **saved back into the knowledge base** — persisted, listed among the fund's documents, part of the record.
- **Should:** ships with trust artifacts — evidence/citations per claim, metadata (who/what/when/from-which-sources), flags ("only one independent reference behind this section"), suggested next steps.
- **Could:** the saved document is itself re-ingested and citable in later conversations (full loop).

## Pillar 4 — Dashboard ("deliberately the loosest pillar — the pure product-taste read")
- **Must:** one view showing state of the world: what's in the KB, what the pipeline is doing, what's been generated.
- **Should:** answers "what's new, what needs me?" — not a wall of internals.
- **Could:** whatever a talent partner would actually want.

## Definition of done
- SPEC.md: "A **thin slice, end to end**: corpus ingested → a grounded, cited conversation → one document generated and saved → visible on a dashboard. All four pillars touched at *must* level beats any pillar polished to *could*." Cuts expected and graded as decisions; record in DECISIONS.md. "We will run it: clean clone → `make up` → your documented steps… undocumented magic counts against, documented pragmatism counts for."
- README "How you finish": (1) clean clone + `make up` + README-documented steps brings the product up — run instructions at the top of `DECISIONS.md` or a `RUNNING.md`; (2) commit and push everything including DECISIONS.md and PROMPTS.md; (3) reply to invite email with repo link and book the 60-min review (demo + one small live change to the codebase together).

## Timebox — 2 to 3 hours ("We mean it")
- ~20–30 min: read SPEC.md, interrogate `context-brain/`, ask questions, decide use case and cuts.
- ~1.5–2 hrs: build the slice.
- ~15–20 min: wrap — DECISIONS.md, PROMPTS.md, final `make up`-from-clean check, push.
- "A thin slice that runs end to end beats two pillars gold-plated… Don't gold-plate; stop at the timebox."

## Evaluation criteria (README, 7 items)
1. **Does the slice work?** Clean clone → `make up` → documented steps → ingest, converse, generate, save. "We will run it."
2. **Full-stack judgment.** Sensible schema, pipeline that handles failure, grounding that doesn't lie, coherent front end, multi-service wiring.
3. **Product taste.** Use case chosen and why; what earned the screen; would the output be trusted by its reader. "This is where `context-brain/` pays off."
4. **The questions you asked** — of them, of the brain, in prompts.
5. **Decisions & honesty.** "Claimed-but-broken costs more than cut-and-said-so."
6. **How you drove the AI.** PROMPTS.md + commit history as one story of delegation, verification, override.
7. **How far you took it.** Spec is floor, not ceiling. Strongest submissions add the unasked-for thing: a small design system/component library, a data model rethought from first principles, an extra feature arguing the business case, ICP/market research that visibly shaped calls. "gold-plating is polishing what was asked for; taste is adding the unasked-for thing that matters."

"No hidden tricks, no planted bugs, no points for suffering."

# 6. DOMAIN / CONTEXT-BRAIN

## Mission (`context-brain/mission.md`)
Belief: in PE the highest-leverage decisions are **people decisions**, and they're the least instrumented part of the firm. Product = "a second brain for the fund's people decisions." Vision, one sentence: *"Every people decision a fund makes, made on evidence it can interrogate — and every decision making the next one smarter."*

Three consequences for anything built:
1. **Evidence is the product** — untraceable output is unusable output.
2. **Memory compounds** — anything generated flows back in, doesn't evaporate.
3. **Trust is structural** — isolation and honest "I don't know" are features, not constraints.

Commercially: sells to lower-mid-market and mid-market PE funds; buyer is the fund's talent function; audience is the deal team; expansion runs downward into portcos.

## Product (`00-product-overview.md`)
Two surfaces: **The Second Brain (fund level)** — ingest, cross-portfolio Q&A ("show me every COO we've assessed who scored low on financial rigor"), generates scorecards, assessments, and the talent review; and **The Portco Workspace (portco level, $8–15K/portco)** — scoped view under a fund; portco HR leader sees only their own data; fund talent partner sees across; no portco sees another. That's the expansion motion.

Not an ATS: cares about judgment and memory, not pipeline stages; encodes a methodology; keeps an audit trail. Deliberately does NOT: source/aggregate candidates, make the hire/no-hire call ("a human always decides… customers ask for explainability, not a verdict"), serve non-PE HR.

Load-bearing for engineers: **grounded answers, provenance, isolation** are the product, not features on top.

## ICP (`01-icp.md`)
- Mid-market PE buyout funds, **$500M–$5B AUM**, **10–40 portcos**.
- Economic buyer: fund's **talent function** — Operating Partner for Talent / Head of Talent / Chief Talent Officer (in small funds, a deal partner who owns "people").
- Why they buy: stakes enormous + tooling nonexistent; mis-hire catastrophic (replacing a portfolio CEO mid-hold burns **12–18 months**); every search starts from zero; they must defend decisions to IC and LPs.
- Great fit: repeatable portfolio-wide talent motion; a named accountable person; already spends **$150K+ per senior search**; values explainability/audit; portfolio as the unit.
- Poor fit: one senior hire a year; wants a "verdict machine"; wants sourcing/ATS; single opco with no IC.
- Buying pattern: trust and word of mouth; stalls on **security/compliance review** far more often than price.

## Jobs to be done (`03-jobs-to-be-done.md`)
1. **Define the role** → output a **scorecard** (mission, 3–6 measurable outcomes over 12–18 months, competencies, red flags). "Most searches that fail, fail here."
2. **Assess candidates against it** → same scorecard, real evidence; surfaces thin evidence, interviewer disagreement, uncorroborated claims. "It does not rank-and-pick."
3. **Decide** → the **assessment**, read by a deal partner before approving a hire; its job is honesty, enabling a confident "no".
4. **Defend the decision** → the **defensibility** job; every claim traces to source. "A score that can't be traced is worse than no score — it looks rigorous and isn't."
5. **Monitor portfolio talent** → the **talent review**: every exec across every portco, scored, flight risk / hi-po flagged, mapped to each VCP; read at board meetings and portfolio reviews.

Through-line: **define → assess → decide → defend → monitor**, currency = trustworthy traceable evidence. "provenance is the product, not a nice-to-have."

## How a fund runs a search (`00-product-overview.md`)
1. Define the role (scorecard) → 2. Assess candidates (capture interviews/references, score, surface gaps and interviewer disagreements) → 3. Decide (assessment the deal partners read) → 4. Defend at IC with traceable evidence → 5. Monitor via the talent review.

## How a talent review is read (`05-talent-review.md`)
- **What it is:** portfolio-wide read on leadership health; every exec scored on role competencies with **flight risk** and **high-potential** flagged, mapped to the VCP. Rolls up from scorecards, assessments, reference calls, board reviews.
- **Who reads it, where:** Hema builds/owns it; Dana and GPs read it at the **semi-annual portfolio review** and at **portco board meetings**; informs IC-level conversations. "The reader who matters most is the one who doesn't use the app" — the partner who sees one number in a slide ("COO scores a 3 on Execution, against a target of 5") and must decide what to do.
- **Why defensible is the game:** score must be **interrogable** (unfold into which assessments, references, observed outcomes, down to the source); **a wrong score is worse than no score** (an empty cell prompts a question; a confident wrong number gets acted on); **the evidence is uneven** and "these should not look the same on the page".
- **The provenance problem** (two silent lineage breaks): (1) **identity merge** — two similarly-named execs collapsed into one record, so one person's glowing reference lands on the other's score; (2) **source-reliability blindness** — a candidate-supplied reference weighted equal to an independently back-channeled one. "no status dashboard will ever flag it: every service shows green, the app 'works', and the output is wrong. In this product, 'working' means *the output is true*, not just *the app runs*."
- **What a strong generated document does:** evidence visible next to the score; distinguishes reliability (independent/corroborated vs. self-selected); drill from number to sources and back; surfaces confidence and gaps honestly; treats trust as the feature. "A weak answer adds polish — nicer charts, more filters — without touching the reason the number can't be trusted."

# 7. UX / DESIGN

`DESIGN.md` header: *"One page, directional, non-binding. If your taste beats ours, use yours — and say why in DECISIONS.md. What we're actually grading is whether the product feels like one coherent thing built for a specific person."* The "Starter visual language" table is explicitly labelled **(optional)**. CLAUDE.md echoes: "Brand & product-feel guidance — directional, non-binding."

**Who it must feel right for:** a fund talent partner and the deal partners they answer to — "People who read board packs for a living, distrust dashboards that perform confidence, and will quote your product's output **in an investment-committee meeting**. The register is *calm, evidentiary, expensive* — a well-typeset memo, not a SaaS carnival."

**Product principles (these are the brand):**
1. **Every number can be interrogated** — evidence is one interaction away, never a dead end.
2. **Status is always visible** — ingesting, processing, failed, ready; the user never wonders whether the system is working.
3. **The brain never bluffs** — uncited prose reads differently than cited prose, gaps are stated, and "I don't know" is styled as a first-class answer, not an error.
4. **Quiet surfaces, loud evidence** — chrome recedes; sources, provenance, and flags earn the visual weight.

**Tokens (suggested):**
| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| Surface | warm paper `#FAF8F3`; cards `#FFFFFF`, 1px borders `#E3E0D8` |
| Ink | near-black `#1D2129`; muted `#6B7280` |
| Accent | **one only** — patina green `#2F6F4F` (actions, active states) |
| Signal | amber for attention; `#B3402F` for failure — sparingly ("a flag that's always red is wallpaper") |
| Type | **serif** for headings/documents (Georgia or similar), **system sans** for UI; generated documents should read like *documents*, not chat bubbles |
| Feel | generous whitespace, real tables, **no gradients, no glassmorphism, no emoji in product surfaces** |

**Anti-patterns:** chat-app cosplay (generated document as a giant chat bubble); confidence theater (green checkmarks, 98% scores with nothing behind them); a dashboard of vanity counters ("42 documents!") answering no user question; ten accent colors doing the job of one.

README evaluation item 7 rewards "a small design system or component library instead of default styling" as an unasked-for-but-valued addition.

# 8. CONVENTIONS

## Decision checkpoints (CLAUDE.md, marked IMPORTANT)
"The decisions in this build belong to the **candidate**, not to you. At each checkpoint below, **stop before implementing**: put the decision to them as a direct question, offer the options with trade-offs if useful, and ask for their call **and their reasoning**. Then record both… in `DECISIONS.md` as you go. Do not pick a default and proceed; 'you decide' from the candidate is an answer to note verbatim, not an invitation to skip the checkpoint."

1. **Use case** (before any code) — which document does the brain generate; who exactly reads it; what are they deciding. Push at `context-brain/` if no view formed.
2. **Scope cuts** (right after) — what's being cut in 2–3 hours and why that's the right cut.
3. **Data model** (before the first migration) — how documents, chunks, generated artifacts are organized; where fund-vs-portco provenance lives.
4. **Pipeline shape** (before wiring ingestion) — what's async vs. inline; what happens when a document fails and where a user sees it.
5. **Grounding strategy** (before the agent code) — what context gets retrieved, how citations attach to claims, what happens when the corpus can't support an answer.
6. **The trust surface** (before the generate UX) — what ships around the generated document (metadata, flags, evidence, confidence); what earns the screen for the reader named in checkpoint 1.
7. **Final pass** (before calling it done) — does DECISIONS.md tell the true story; does clean `make up` + documented steps actually work.

Proportionality rule: "one sharp question at the right moment, not a quiz gate on every file." If a call is reversed mid-build, ask what changed and update the log. On a thin answer, probe once ("standard for whom? your reader is a PE partner"), then respect and record.

## Verbatim-quote rule (CLAUDE.md, strongest convention)
"**Record answers verbatim.** When you write a checkpoint decision into `DECISIONS.md`, quote the candidate's actual reply — their words, in quotation marks — not your paraphrase of it. Do not compose, polish, or expand their rationale, and **never fill in the 'In your own words' fields yourself**; those belong to the candidate's keyboard. The reviewers cross-check `DECISIONS.md` quotes against the raw session transcript in `prompts/` — invented or paraphrased quotes hurt the candidate."

DECISIONS.md restates this from the candidate's side, and README adds: "we don't mind who *typed* DECISIONS.md — we care that the thinking is yours… we'll probe your recorded decisions live, ask for the counterfactuals, and cross-reference quotes against your raw transcript."

## DECISIONS.md logging expectations
Keep it as you go, not from memory at the end. Required sections: **How to run what I built** (exact steps from clean clone, followed literally), **The use case I chose**, **Decisions & trade-offs** (one block per significant decision, at minimum the six checkpoint ones: use case, cuts, data model, pipeline shape, grounding, trust surface), **What I cut**, **If I had another day**. Per-decision block format:
```
### Decision: …
- **The call:** what you chose
- **Said at the time:** "…" (verbatim, captured by your agent from the conversation)
- **What I gave up:** the trade-off
- **In your own words (typed by you, not your agent):** why this was right
```
"Cuts recorded here are graded as product decisions; things silently missing are graded as gaps."

## PROMPTS.md logging expectations
Honest, lightweight, as-you-go. Per-exchange format:
```
## [time] tool: claude-code
**Asked:** paste or summarize the prompt
**Got:** one line on what came back
**Did with it:** took it / rejected it because … / redirected it by …
```
Reading for: what was **delegated** vs. kept; whether output was **verified** and how; where the tool was **overridden or redirected**; what was asked to **understand the customer and problem**, not just produce code. Includes questions asked of `context-brain/`, of tools about the problem, and of the company by email. Raw session exports go in `prompts/` as-is — "**We treat the raw log as the source of truth**" and PROMPTS.md is the annotated index. "Don't sanitize the export: dead ends, tool errors, and wrong turns read as experience, not failure. A trail with no wrong turns and no timestamps reads as reconstructed."

## Grounding / citation rules (repeated in four files)
- SPEC: citations must **trace to a real passage** — "a reader can open the source and find the line"; when the KB lacks the answer the brain says so and never invents.
- STACK: "**The brain never lies.** No citation, no claim. 'I don't know' is a feature."
- DESIGN: "The brain never bluffs" — uncited prose reads differently than cited, gaps stated, "I don't know" styled as a first-class answer, not an error.
- CLAUDE.md: "**Grounding is non-negotiable.** … No citation, no claim."

## Other working rules (CLAUDE.md "How to help well")
- **Push understanding before code** — suggest ten minutes in `context-brain/` and SPEC.md before "build the spec".
- **Respect the rails** — technology families fixed; don't swap frameworks or reach for external services; only external dependency is the Anthropic API.
- **Thin slice over broad shell** — flag scope creep; 2–3 hour timebox.
- **It must run on a stranger's machine** — re-verify clean clone → `make up` → documented steps before calling it done.
- Everything is fictional; local experimentation is safe; `make reset` wipes the backing services.
- Secrets stay out of git (`.env` gitignored).
- Ownership rule (README): "**You own every line.** AI output you didn't verify, understand, or would not defend in review is the single failure mode we screen hardest for."

# Project brief

## What this is

- A take-home **build challenge**: build a working slice of "the Second Brain" — a document-intelligence product for a fictional PE fund, **DAW Capital** — from a product spec, against pre-wired empty infra. No starter app exists.
- Goal for the assisting agent: help the candidate build **their** design well, not substitute for their product thinking. See decision-checkpoint protocol in [[conventions]].

## Customer / product (see [[business-logic]] for full domain model)

- Belief: PE people-decisions are high-stakes and least-instrumented. Product = "a second brain for the fund's people decisions."
- Two surfaces: **The Second Brain** (fund level — ingest, cross-portfolio Q&A, generates scorecards/assessments/talent review) and **The Portco Workspace** ($8–15K/portco — scoped, isolated view for a portco HR leader). Expansion motion runs fund → portco.
- Not an ATS: no sourcing, no hire/no-hire verdict (human always decides), no non-PE HR.
- ICP: mid-market PE buyout funds, $500M–$5B AUM, 10–40 portcos. Economic buyer: the fund's talent function.

## The four pillars (must build a thin slice across all four)

1. **Ingest** — async ingestion of `data/` corpus (fund + 3 portcos) into a retrieval-capable KB; per-document status queued/processing/ready/failed; a bad file fails *that document*, visibly.
2. **Converse** — chat grounded in ingested docs with citations tracing to a real passage; says "I don't know" when the KB lacks the answer.
3. **Generate** *(the heart of the exercise)* — from chat, generate one document type (candidate profile / search comparison / exec-or-portco brief — pick one), grounded in the KB, and **save it back into the KB** as part of the record.
4. **Dashboard** — one view of KB state, pipeline activity, and what's been generated. Loosest pillar, pure product-taste read.

Full must/should/could tiers and grounding/isolation rules: [[business-logic]].

## Definition of done

- A thin slice, end to end: corpus ingested → grounded cited conversation → one document generated and saved → visible on dashboard. **All four pillars at must** beats any one pillar gold-plated.
- Timebox: **2–3 hours** ("we mean it"). ~20–30 min spec/context-brain interrogation + deciding use case/cuts, ~1.5–2h build, ~15–20 min wrap (DECISIONS.md, PROMPTS.md, clean-`make up` check, push).
- Must run on a stranger's machine: clean clone → `make up` → steps documented in DECISIONS.md.
- Commit and push everything including DECISIONS.md and PROMPTS.md; reply to invite email with repo link; book 60-min review (demo + one small live change together).

## Evaluation criteria (7 items, from README)

1. Does the slice work — will they run it and get ingest→converse→generate→save→dashboard?
2. Full-stack judgment — schema, failure-handling pipeline, non-lying grounding, coherent front end, service wiring.
3. Product taste — use case chosen and why, what earned the screen, would the reader trust it (this is where `context-brain/` pays off).
4. The questions asked — of context-brain, of the brain, in prompts.
5. Decisions & honesty — "claimed-but-broken costs more than cut-and-said-so."
6. How the AI was driven — PROMPTS.md + commits as one story of delegation/verification/override.
7. How far it was taken — spec is floor not ceiling; strongest submissions add the unasked-for thing (design system, rethought data model, business-case feature, ICP research that shaped calls).

"No hidden tricks, no planted bugs, no points for suffering."

## Non-goals / explicit cuts already known to be out of scope for a v1

- Not building all three generate-document types — one use case is enough.
- Auth/RLS-enforced org isolation, streaming, reranking, DLQ, re-ingesting the generated doc — all **could**-tier, expected to be cut under the timebox (see candidate's actual cut list once recorded in DECISIONS.md).

# Business logic

## Domain chain (jobs to be done)

**Define → Assess → Decide → Defend → Monitor**, currency throughout = trustworthy, traceable evidence.

1. **Define the role** → output a **scorecard** (mission, 3–6 measurable outcomes over 12–18mo, competencies, red flags). "Most searches that fail, fail here."
2. **Assess candidates** against that scorecard with real evidence; surfaces thin evidence, interviewer disagreement, uncorroborated claims. Does not rank-and-pick.
3. **Decide** → the **assessment**, read by a deal partner before approving a hire; job is honesty, enabling a confident "no".
4. **Defend the decision** at IC — every claim traces to source. "A score that can't be traced is worse than no score — it looks rigorous and isn't."
5. **Monitor portfolio talent** → the **talent review**: every exec across every portco, scored, flight-risk/hi-po flagged, mapped to the VCP; read at board meetings and portfolio reviews.

## Personas (who the product must satisfy)

| Persona | Role | Stake |
|---|---|---|
| **Hema Varadarajan** — Talent Partner | Primary user & buyer, Operating Partner (Human Capital & Talent), DAW Capital | Runs 6–10 senior searches/yr; needs leverage + IC-defensible evidence; fears a confident wrong answer she repeats to a deal partner |
| **Marcus Boone** — Portco HR Leader | Secondary, VP People, Cascade Care Group | Scoped to Cascade only; fears leakage to a peer portco — "he is the reason isolation is non-negotiable" |
| **Dana Deline** — Deal Partner / GP | IC audience, IC chair | Rarely logs in, sees output secondhand; needs a trustworthy decision in ~10 min with evidence to point to — "the output has to carry its own credibility" |
| **Sam Iyer** — Talent Associate | Power user | Uploads, chases references, drafts first passes; fears **silent failures** — "feels every pipeline glitch first" |

Rule of thumb: a feature that helps Sam produce what Hema can defend to Dana is on the money. Something that breaks the app is loud; something that quietly makes an output *wrong* costs the most.

## Accounts / tenancy

- **DAW Capital** — the fund, lower-middle-market buyout, ~$680M AUM, Denver. Talent function: Hema + Sam; IC chaired by Dana.
- **Three portcos = three separate tenants** — provenance belongs in the data model from the first migration:
  - **PC1 Vantage Managed Services** (IT/MSP) — CTO flight-risk is top EV exposure.

# Stack and deps

## Mandated technology families (fixed — "the constraint is the exercise")

| Layer | Constraint |
|---|---|
| Frontend | React 18 + Vite, TanStack Query for server state. Component library/styling: free choice |
| API | Node/TypeScript-or-JS HTTP service. STACK.md example: Hono (Express/Fastify also fine). Postgres access method free |
| Knowledge base | Postgres + pgvector for chunks/embeddings/metadata. Schema is a first-class deliverable |
| Pipeline | MinIO object storage + ElasticMQ queue, async workers, via AWS SDKs (S3/SQS) pointed at local endpoints, `forcePathStyle: true` for MinIO. A pipeline that skips the queue and does everything inline misses the point of the pillar |
| AI layer | Anthropic for generation/conversation, via LangChain/LangGraph or equivalent agent structure (hand-rolled allowed if justified). Embeddings: free choice, hosted or local/deterministic — "the corpus is small; simple works" |
| Runtime | Everything locally under Docker; compose for services, app in containers or on host (must be documented). **Only external dependency allowed: the Anthropic API** |

**Explicit bans:** no Next.js-on-Vercel, no Pinecone, no Redis-as-the-queue. Beyond these families, any library is allowed.

## Backing services (docker-compose.yml, project name `second-brain`)

| Service | Image | Port(s) | Credentials | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `db` | `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` | `5432` | user `brain` / pass `brain` / db `secondbrain` | healthcheck `pg_isready`; volume `pgdata` |
| `minio` | `minio/minio:latest` | `9000` API / `9001` console | `minio-root` / `minio-secret` | `server /data --console-address ":9001"`; healthcheck `mc ready local`; volume `miniodata` |
| `queue` | `softwaremill/elasticmq-native:latest` | `9324` (SQS-compatible) | any creds work locally | no healthcheck, no volume — ephemeral |

All three start **empty**: no schema, no buckets, no queues — the candidate provisions them.

- In-container hostnames: `db`, `minio`, `queue` (vs. `localhost` from the host).
- Connection strings: Postgres `postgres://brain:brain@localhost:5432/secondbrain`; MinIO API `http://localhost:9000`.

## Env

- `.env.example` declares one var: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` — "the only external dependency; everything else runs locally in Docker."
- `.env` is gitignored; copy from `.env.example` and paste the scoped, spend-capped key.

## "Production-shaped" — five habits (STACK.md)

1. Isolation is a data-layer concern — fund vs. portco provenance in the schema, not scattered `if` statements (full RLS enforcement = could; thinking about it = must).
2. Async work fails visibly — status fields / dashboard tile, not only logs.
3. The brain never lies — no citation, no claim.
4. Secrets stay out of git.
5. It runs on a stranger's machine — clean clone → `make up` → documented steps.

## Current state of app-level dependencies

- **No `package.json`, no lockfile, no `Dockerfile`, no `tsconfig.json` exist yet** — this is a pre-code planning-stage repo (only spec/infra/corpus/docs are committed).
- Planning-conversation direction (not yet implemented, see [[active-context]]): monorepo `apps/web` (React 18 + Vite + TanStack Query) + `apps/backend` (single image, `start:api` / `start:worker` commands) with Hono, AWS SDK v3 for S3/SQS, local embeddings via `@xenova/transformers` MiniLM → `vector(384)` in pgvector. No `packages/` planned.

# Architecture

## Current state

**No application code exists yet.** No `apps/`, `packages/`, migrations, Dockerfiles, or frontend. The repo is spec + infra + corpus + docs only (one commit: `feat: init repo`). Everything below the "Planned shape" heading is direction reached in planning conversation, not yet built — verify against actual code before trusting it.

## Planned shape (from candidate's planning conversation, not yet implemented)

- **Monorepo**: `apps/web` (React 18 + Vite + TanStack Query) + `apps/backend` (single image, two entry commands: `start:api` and `start:worker` sharing the same codebase). No `packages/` planned as unnecessary for this scope.
- **Backend internals**: Hono API; SQS-polling-loop worker; shared libs under `src/lib/{db,s3,sqs,embed,anthropic}.ts`; `src/schemas/`; `src/prompts/`; `src/db/` for raw SQL/migrations.
- **Data model sketch**:
  - `orgs(id)` — fund + each portco as a row.
  - `documents(id, org_id, origin, doc_kind, title, status, error, s3_key, body, conversation_id, …)` — `origin` distinguishes seeded vs. uploaded vs. generated; `status` carries queued/processing/ready/failed.
  - `chunks(id, document_id, org_id, ordinal, content, embedding vector(384))` — `org_id` denormalized onto chunks for isolation-by-query without a join.
  - `conversations(id, org_ids[])`, `messages(id, conversation_id, role, content, citation_ids, …)`.
- **Ingest flow**: seed/upload → `PutObject` to MinIO → `INSERT documents` (status `queued`) → `SendMessage` SQS `{documentId}` → worker: `processing` → `GetObject` → non-`.md` file ⇒ `failed` (visible, not a pipeline crash) → parse YAML frontmatter + split on `##` headers → embed chunks → `INSERT chunks` → `ready`. Office-format duplicates (`.docx/.pptx/.xlsx`) are the deliberate "unsupported format" failure case, not seeded as primary content.
- **Converse flow**: synchronous `POST /conversations/:id/messages` → embed question → `SELECT chunks WHERE org_id = ANY(conversation.org_ids) ORDER BY embedding <=> query LIMIT 20` → 0 chunks ⇒ respond "not in the KB" → else Claude call → `{answer, citationIds}`. A conversation is not locked to one org; a multi-select org filter scopes retrieval per turn.
- **Generate flow**: synchronous `POST /conversations/:id/portco-briefs {orgId}` (orgId must be one of the conversation's org_ids) → retrieve only that org's chunks → Claude with an IC-facing system prompt + a `portco-brief-v1` JSON schema → validate returned `citationIds ⊆` chunks actually sent → `INSERT documents(origin=generated, doc_kind=portco_brief, body jsonb, status=ready)`. Markdown export is a deterministic JSON→markdown render, not a second Claude call. Re-ingesting the generated brief is a cut (could-tier).
- **Frontend surfaces**: Documents list (upload + generated, origin filter, pipeline status, download, org); Chat (org filter + "Generate brief" action); Brief view (rendered JSON sections with clickable inline citations). Dashboard-must may reuse the Documents page plus status counters (ready / in-flight / failed / N briefs generated).

## Isolation / provenance

Fund-vs-portco provenance must live in the schema (`org_id` on documents and chunks), not in scattered application-level `if` statements — this is graded as a data-model decision (see decision checkpoint 3 in [[conventions]]). Full RLS enforcement is could-tier; the schema shape itself is must-tier.

## Grounding / citation mechanics

- Retrieval scope is always org-filtered (`org_id = ANY(...)`), never global, to respect tenancy.
- Citations are chunk IDs returned by Claude and validated server-side against the chunk set actually sent in the prompt — never trust an unvalidated citation ID back from the model.
- Zero retrieved chunks is a valid, expected state → answer must be "not in the KB", not a hallucinated guess.

# Conventions

## Decision-checkpoint protocol (IMPORTANT — this governs how the assisting agent must behave)

The decisions in this build belong to the **candidate**, not the agent. At each checkpoint below: **stop before implementing**, ask the decision as a direct question (offer trade-offs if useful), get the candidate's call **and their reasoning**, then record both in DECISIONS.md. Never pick a default and proceed silently — "you decide" from the candidate is itself an answer to record verbatim, not permission to skip the checkpoint.

The seven checkpoints:

1. **Use case** (before any code) — which document the brain generates, who reads it, what they're deciding. Push toward `context-brain/` if the candidate hasn't formed a view.
2. **Scope cuts** (right after) — what's cut for the 2–3hr timebox and why that's the right cut.
3. **Data model** (before the first migration) — how documents/chunks/generated artifacts are organized, where fund-vs-portco provenance lives.
4. **Pipeline shape** (before wiring ingestion) — what's async vs. inline, what happens on document failure and where the user sees it.
5. **Grounding strategy** (before agent code) — what gets retrieved, how citations attach to claims, behavior when the corpus can't support an answer.
6. **The trust surface** (before the generate UX) — what ships around the generated doc (metadata, flags, evidence, confidence); what earns the screen for the checkpoint-1 reader.
7. **Final pass** (before calling it done) — does DECISIONS.md tell the true story; does clean `make up` + documented steps actually work.

Proportionality: one sharp question at the right moment, not a quiz gate on every file. If the candidate reverses an earlier call mid-build, ask what changed and update the log. On a thin answer ("just do whatever's standard"), probe once ("standard for whom? your reader is a PE partner"), then respect their call and record it.

## Verbatim-quote rule (strongest convention — violating this hurts the candidate's grade)

When writing a checkpoint decision into DECISIONS.md, quote the candidate's **actual words**, in quotation marks — never paraphrase, compose, polish, or expand their rationale. **Never fill in the "In your own words" field** — that belongs to the candidate's own keyboard. Reviewers cross-check DECISIONS.md quotes against the raw session transcript in `prompts/`; invented or paraphrased quotes cost the candidate.

## DECISIONS.md required structure

- **How to run what I built** — exact steps from clean clone, meant to be followed literally.
- **The use case I chose**.
- **Decisions & trade-offs** — one block per significant decision, at minimum the six checkpoint decisions (use case, cuts, data model, pipeline shape, grounding, trust surface). Per-decision block:
  ```
  ### Decision: …
  - **The call:** what you chose
  - **Said at the time:** "…" (verbatim, captured by the agent from conversation)
  - **What I gave up:** the trade-off
  - **In your own words (typed by you, not your agent):** why this was right
  ```
- **What I cut**.
- **If I had another day**.

Cuts recorded here are graded as product decisions; things silently missing are graded as gaps.

## PROMPTS.md required structure

Honest, lightweight, logged **as-you-go**, not reconstructed at the end. Per-exchange:
```
## [time] tool: claude-code
**Asked:** paste or summarize the prompt
**Got:** one line on what came back
**Did with it:** took it / rejected it because … / redirected it by …
```
Include questions asked of `context-brain/`, of tools about the problem, and of the company by email — not just code prompts. Raw session exports (`prompts/raw-session-*.jsonl`, auto-exported by the Stop/SessionEnd hooks) are the **source of truth**; PROMPTS.md is the annotated index. Don't sanitize the export — dead ends, tool errors, wrong turns read as experience, not failure. A trail with no wrong turns and no timestamps reads as reconstructed.

## Grounding / citation rule (hard, repeated across README/SPEC/STACK/DESIGN)

No citation, no claim. Citations must trace to a real passage a reader can open and find. When the KB is silent, say so — "I don't know" is a feature, not an error. See [[business-logic]] for the product-level rationale and [[architecture]] for the citation-validation mechanics.

## How to help well (agent behavior rules)

- **Push understanding before code.** If the candidate jumps to "build the spec," suggest ten minutes in `context-brain/` and SPEC.md first — use-case choice and cuts are graded. Their questions are part of the assessment; encourage logging good ones in PROMPTS.md.
- **Respect the rails.** Technology families in [[stack-and-deps]] are fixed. Don't swap frameworks or reach for external services — only external dependency is the Anthropic API.
- **Thin slice over broad shell.** All four pillars at must beats any pillar gold-plated. Flag scope creep against the 2–3hr timebox.
- **It must run on a stranger's machine.** Re-verify clean clone → `make up` → documented steps before the candidate calls it done.
- Everything is fictional; local experimentation is safe; `make reset` wipes backing services clean.
- Ownership rule (README): "You own every line." AI output the candidate didn't verify, understand, or wouldn't defend in review is the top failure mode graders screen for.

## Repo hygiene

- `.claude/settings.json` wires Stop + SessionEnd hooks to `scripts/export-transcript.sh`, which copies the running transcript to `prompts/raw-session-<id>.jsonl` on every session end — this is automatic; just make sure those files get committed, don't hand-edit them.

# UX direction

Status: **directional, non-binding** (DESIGN.md's own framing). "If your taste beats ours, use yours — and say why in DECISIONS.md." What's actually graded is whether the product feels like one coherent thing built for a specific person.

## Who it must feel right for

A fund talent partner (Hema) and the deal partners she answers to (Dana) — people who read board packs for a living, distrust dashboards that perform confidence, and may quote the product's output **in an investment-committee meeting**. Register: **calm, evidentiary, expensive** — a well-typeset memo, not a SaaS carnival.

## Product principles (these ARE the brand)

1. **Every number can be interrogated** — evidence is one interaction away, never a dead end.
2. **Status is always visible** — ingesting/processing/failed/ready; the user never wonders if the system is working.
3. **The brain never bluffs** — uncited prose reads differently than cited prose; gaps are stated; "I don't know" is styled as a first-class answer, not an error.
4. **Quiet surfaces, loud evidence** — chrome recedes; sources, provenance, and flags earn the visual weight.

# tt-challenges — Second Brain build challenge

Take-home build challenge: build a working slice of "the Second Brain" (a document-intelligence product for fictional PE fund **DAW Capital**) from a product spec, against pre-wired empty infra. No starter app — the candidate builds **their** design; help them build it well, don't substitute for their product thinking.

## Commands

```bash
make up              # docker compose up -d --build — starts db/minio/queue, all empty. THE entry point.
make down            # stop services, keep volumes
make reset           # down -v then up — wipe and restart clean
make ps              # container states
make logs [SVC=name] # tail logs, all services or one (db|minio|queue)
make psql            # psql shell into db (brain/brain, db secondbrain)
make help            # list targets
```

No `package.json` / lint / test / build commands exist yet — no application code has been written (see [[active-context]]).

## Environment

| Var | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Only external dependency. Copy `.env.example` → `.env` (gitignored) and paste the scoped key. |

| Service | Endpoint | Credentials |
|---|---|---|
| Postgres + pgvector | `localhost:5432`, db `secondbrain` | `brain` / `brain` |
| MinIO (S3) | API `localhost:9000`, console `localhost:9001` | `minio-root` / `minio-secret` |
| ElasticMQ (SQS) | `localhost:9324` | any |

All three start empty — schema, buckets, queues are the candidate's to build.

## Architecture (summary)

No app code exists yet. Planned (not yet built — see [[architecture]] for full detail and [[active-context]] for what's actually confirmed vs. still just discussed): monorepo `apps/web` (React+Vite+TanStack Query) + `apps/backend` (Hono API + SQS worker, one image), Postgres+pgvector KB with `org_id`-scoped `documents`/`chunks`, MinIO for raw objects, ElasticMQ for async ingest jobs, Anthropic for chat + generation.

## Decision checkpoints — the core behavioral contract of this repo (IMPORTANT)

The build decisions belong to the **candidate**, not the assisting agent. At each of the 7 checkpoints (use case → scope cuts → data model → pipeline shape → grounding strategy → trust surface → final pass), **stop before implementing**, ask directly, get their call **and reasoning**, then record both **verbatim** in DECISIONS.md — never paraphrase or fill in "in your own words" yourself. Full checkpoint list, the verbatim-quote rule, and DECISIONS.md/PROMPTS.md required formats: [[conventions]].

## Verification

Before calling anything done: clean clone → `make up` → the steps documented in DECISIONS.md must actually bring the product up and let a stranger ingest → converse → generate → see it on the dashboard. Undocumented magic counts against; documented pragmatism counts for.

## Memory

Deep knowledge lives in `.claude/memory/`. Read relevant files when working in those areas — don't load all of them every session.

| File | Contains | Read when |
|------|----------|-----------|
| project-brief.md | Mission, four pillars, timebox, evaluation criteria | Scope questions, "what are we even building" |
| architecture.md | Data model, ingest/converse/generate flow, isolation mechanics | Structural/schema/pipeline work |
| conventions.md | Decision-checkpoint protocol, verbatim-quote rule, DECISIONS.md/PROMPTS.md formats, grounding rule | Every session start; any time a checkpoint may apply |
| business-logic.md | Personas, JTBD chain, DAW/portco tenancy, corpus structure, grounding invariant | Domain/product questions, generate-pillar work |
| ux-direction.md | Brand register, tokens, anti-patterns (non-binding) | UI work |
| stack-and-deps.md | Fixed tech families, backing-service config, banned choices | Adding deps, infra config |
| active-context.md | What's actually built vs. only discussed, next steps, open questions | Session start, before trusting any "decided" fact |
